title: Academic 01 Speaking — source-based review candidate
instructions: Answer the interviewer's questions in English.
In Part 2, you have one minute to prepare and can make notes. Then speak for up to two minutes.
The interviewer may ask follow-up questions.

timing.note: Select a coherent run within 11–14 minutes; do not add independent maximums as a mandatory duration.

parts.instructions: Answer questions about familiar topics. The interviewer chooses an appropriate selection and follows up where useful.
opening: What name would you like me to use?
Do you work, study, or do something else at the moment?

questions: What do you tend to do in your town or city at weekends?
Tell me about the last time you went to the countryside.
Which local activities do you enjoy most?
Has your hairstyle changed much in recent years?
How do you feel about trying a different hair colour?
What do you like or dislike about having your hair cut?

followUpPrompts: Can you tell me a little more?
parts.interviewerGuidance: Use a natural selection within 4–5 minutes. Do not demand every question if time is reached; do not coach or correct during the attempt.

parts.instructions: You have one minute to prepare. You can make notes. Then speak for up to two minutes.

cueCard.topic: Describe an occasion when you used information intended for visitors to a place.
cueCard.explain: Explain how useful this information was to you.

roundingOffQuestions: Would you use that source of visitor information again?
Did you share the information with anyone?
parts.interviewerGuidance: Allow exactly one minute preparation under standard practice conditions. Invite the long turn, allow up to two minutes, and stop politely at the limit. Use one or two short rounding-off questions as appropriate; preserve 3–4 minutes for Part 2 including preparation. If the learner stops early, invite continuation neutrally without supplying content.

parts.instructions: Discuss wider questions about holidays and visitor attractions.

questions.question: What kinds of holiday are especially common among people where you live?
neutralProbes: Why might these appeal to different people?

questions.question: Why might someone choose a trip within their own country instead of travelling abroad?
neutralProbes: Could the reasons differ at different times in life?

questions.question: Why do some holidaymakers prefer rest to a busy programme of activities?
neutralProbes: Could one type of holiday suit everyone?

questions.question: What can cause visitors to feel let down by an attraction?
neutralProbes: How might expectations affect the experience?
Could better visitor information change the outcome?

questions.question: Should residents be able to enter local museums without paying?
neutralProbes: Who might benefit, and what difficulties could arise?
Would your answer be the same for every museum?

parts.interviewerGuidance: Select questions and responsive neutral probes to explore explanation, comparison and speculation within 4–5 minutes. Do not supply arguments, vocabulary or an ideal answer. Do not mechanically read every probe. The discussion relates to Part 2 but moves to general issues.

teacherOnly.release: Restricted reviewer guide; no pre-submit coaching/answer guidance in independent conditions.

rubric.sourceVersion: Current official public Speaking descriptors, accessed 2026-11-06
rubric.scope: Performance across the interview; do not average three invented part bands.
rubric.numericBandPolicy: No band estimates in this review edition.

intendedEvidence.part1: Relevant answers and accessible expansion on familiar experience.
intendedEvidence.part2: Organisation and sustained speech from brief notes, with specific relevant details.
intendedEvidence.part3: Responsive explanation, analysis, comparison and qualified speculation.
intendedEvidence.audio: Preserve pauses, self-repair, rhythm, stress, intonation and intelligibility; transcript alone is insufficient.

interviewerPolicy.actor: Human IELTS teacher/interviewer for review; any AI interviewer needs separate reviewed policy and evaluation.
interviewerPolicy.followUps: Responsive neutral requests for elaboration; not hints that introduce answer content.
interviewerPolicy.accessArrangements: Define reviewed alternate conditions explicitly; never infer weak ability from an accommodation.
interviewerPolicy.interruption: Save actual audio and timestamps. Mark material interruption/failed capture; do not silently count the run as standard-condition evidence.

insufficientEvidence: Capture ends before sufficient connected speech is available.
Only transcript exists for a pronunciation judgement.
Interviewer supplies substantive content or corrects language during the independent attempt.
feedbackRules: Quote a real transcript span where relevant and attach the audio timecode.
Listen to original audio before pronunciation/fluency observations; report uncertain ASR text as uncertain.
Prioritise a concrete repair task without treating accent imitation, speed or number of advanced words as a score.
Keep sensitive personal disclosures out of examples and reports.
reviewQuestions: Do actual source topics remain faithfully transformed rather than replaced by unrelated invention?
Do personal Part1 questions stay distinct from abstract Part3 demands?
Does Part3 retain the tourism link to the visitor-information long turn?
Can a responsive interviewer administer a selection within11–14minutes without coaching?
Has source-family overlap with training/transfer material been reviewed before independent admission?
preReleaseChecks: Named IELTS teacher reviews complete guide and performs a synthetic timed administration.
Obtain consent and data controls for any later learner recordings.
Implement recording, replay, durable save, microphone error and interrupted-attempt recovery.
Keep teacher-only guidance out of learner/tutor independent context.
